Their narration and any surfaced witness quotes are verbatim-accurate — quote them as-is — but a stub carries no provenance (source, date, supersession). Expand (aswritten_expand with the IRIs you need) before any claim that turns on WHEN or by WHOM something was said, or whether it is still the current framing. Witness-depth sections below already carry full provenance.

Expand a subtree when its narration (or name) shows your subject plausibly lives there — you'll get the trajectory, the variants, and the verbatim witness. positions.name: OwnedVsRentedIntelligence
positions.frame: What is the constitutive distinction between owned and rented intelligence, and what does each frame retain versus commodify?
positions.why: The directional reads converge across every dimension: both perform the same aphoristic-technical-maxim register, both appeal to autonomy and self-enhancement as the retained good, both assert market-pricing proportionality without naming a price, and both state the distinction as axiomatic principle rather than argued claim. src-2 names the owned/rented opposition directly; src-3 restates it through the commodity/asset metaphor — substrate is commodity, perspective is the asset kept. The set holds no internal tension; src-3 is a creedal restatement of src-2's thesis.

positions.name: DocumentSelfDescribedPurpose
positions.frame: What is this document's self-described function within the extraction pipeline?
positions.why: Both expressions are meta-commentary in which the e2e harness describes what the document is for: src-1 identifies it as a positioning note for a navigation/provenance regression guard, src-4 explains it restates the individually-owned-intelligence thesis so a navigating extractor has existing positioning to connect to. Both share the claim conviction level — flat descriptive assertions, not creedal — and both occupy the same footing (e2e harness as author and animator). The set holds a mild tension: src-1 frames the document's purpose as tooling infrastructure (regression guard), while src-4 frames it as thesis positioning for an extractor — the document serves both mechanical and semantic functions simultaneously.

placements.title: owned intelligence retains what rented intelligence commodifies
placements.frame: What does an intelligence owner retain that a renter does not, and how does that distinction reframe substrate versus perspective?
placements.why: src-2 and src-3 carry the same constitutive thesis — owned vs rented intelligence, substrate as commodity, perspective as the retained asset — performed as axiomatic principle across every dimensional read. No existing leaf or strata holds this. The grain test admits it: this names a subject (the individually-owned-intelligence thesis) that future envelopes will keep feeding, not a one-time fact or measurement.
